analysis: Digestion of disaccharides primarily occurs in the small intestine. This is where enzymes such as lactase, sucrase, and maltase are secreted by the intestinal lining to break down disaccharides into monosaccharides, which can then be absorbed. The retrieved medical knowledge mentions the duodenum, which is part of the small intestine, as a location of disaccharides, supporting the idea that disaccharide digestion occurs there. The other options (mouth, stomach, and large intestine) do not primarily involve the digestion of disaccharides, as the necessary enzymes are not active or present in significant amounts in these locations.
